forward_finding: Before f even lands: the Janus does NOT escape the U–f trade-off, it is the other END of it. Interlayer = dark + big dipole (fails on f). Janus = bright + tiny dipole (U_dip ≈ 0.005–0.09 meV ≪ 7.5 meV need). The BSE will confirm MoSSe is bright, but its DIPOLAR blockade U is structurally far too small. So Janus is not a new dipolar door — it's a bright TMD whose only blockade route is the same saturation/moiré single-emitter leg as MoS2.

verdict: Janus dipolar-blockade route CLOSES on U (tiny dipole). MoSSe remains a bright, tightly-bound TMD → its blockade hope is the saturation/moiré single-emitter leg, already characterized as open-but-single-emitter. The solve-for-it 'escape' was half right (bright ✓) and half wrong (dipole ✗).
